candidates.title: Three LLM inflection points in twelve months
candidates.author: Simon Willison
candidates.event_date: Keynote at AI Engineer Code Summit 'a couple of weeks ago' (exact date UNVERIFIED)
candidates.what_changed: Willison frames the past year of coding agents as three capability inflection points and asks whether Fable 5.2 is a fourth.
candidates.mechanism: Practitioner retrospective tied to concrete projects: default-correct coding (Opus 4.5 / GPT-5.1-Codex, Nov 2025), 'Fable class' proactive goal-driven agents (Jun/Jul 2026), 3D modeling and game design / 'understanding fun' (Opus 5.5, Sep/Oct 2026).
candidates.evidence_quality: Single expert's experience; anecdotal but specific (named releases, project examples). No controlled measurements.
candidates.independent_confirmation: Partial: timeline of model releases is public; claims about capability are personal judgment.
candidates.relevance: Medium-high: useful framing for readers deciding how much autonomy to hand coding agents; 'give it a goal, give it the right tools, and watch it cook'.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: None directly; prior issues covered Simon's sandboxing and GPT-6.2 Astra posts, not this retrospective.
candidates.summary: Published on the one-year anniversary of Claude Opus 4.5 (Nov 24 2025). Inflection 1 (Nov 2025): Opus 4.5 was the first model where Claude Code's default result was 'generally the right thing'; before that he did not use Claude Code as a daily driver because he had to correct it too often. GPT-5.1 / GPT-5.1-Codex / Codex-Max had the same effect on Codex. People tinkered over December and used them for real work by January. Claude Code was 9 months old then (launched Feb 24 2025 with Claude 3.7 Sonnet). Inflection 2 (June/July 2026): Claude Mythos announced in April as too dangerous (could find and exploit vulns); Claude Fable 5 released in June as 'a defanged Mythos' that blocks security work; placed under US export controls after three days, back July 1. He defines 'Fable class' models (definition list did not render in fetch) by examples: Fable spun up its own pyobjc Quartz screenshot mechanism and a CORS-enabled localhost logging server to debug a Safari glitch; with five WebAudio microphones, Opus 5.5 then Fable 5.2 triangulated a mysterious beep to within ~40cm. Classes Fable 5/5.1/5.2 and Opus 5.5 ('cheap Fable') as Fable class; GPT-6 Astra too; Gemini 4 Neon 'may count'. These are now his baseline expectation. Inflection 3 (Sep/Oct 2026): frontier models got good at 3D modeling (Blender, Three.js) - noted with Fable 5, accelerated with Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 4. In August a Fable 5 raccoon heist game played poorly; GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra better but dull after 90 seconds. Prompting Opus 5.5 'This game isn't fun enough yet. Make it a LOT more fun.' worked: his C&C-style RTS went from boring to entertaining after Opus spent 12 hours playtesting and rebalancing. Opus 5.5 released Sep 22 2026. Is Fable 5.2 a fourth? It 'seems to have taste that almost exactly matches my own'; in three weeks he shipped Datasette 1.0a42-a44 and LLM 0.37-0.38 (5 releases). Possible key feature: 'if you can imagine and then clearly describe a piece of software, Fable can build it.' Closes: 'I don't think I'll ever go back to typing most of my code by hand.' Video of talk linked from post (not watched).

candidates.title: Ladybird's first alpha release (and coding agents adding 75,650 WPT passes)
candidates.author: Simon Willison
candidates.event_date: Ladybird alpha released 2026-11-23 ('This morning'); WPT surge Oct 22-27 2026
candidates.what_changed: Ladybird browser shipped its first installable alpha (macOS/Linux); Willison highlights that much of October's progress came from pointing coding agents at the web-platform-tests suite.
candidates.mechanism: Agents used a large conformance test suite (WPT, ~2.25M subtests) as the target/oracle: 'We pointed AI coding agents at WPT and asked them to fill in missing functionality. They made lots of small fixes, and those added up.'
candidates.evidence_quality: Quoted figures from Ladybird's 'This Month in Ladybird - October 2026' (primary not fetched by me); Simon's own hands-on testing.
candidates.independent_confirmation: UNVERIFIED beyond Simon quoting the Ladybird newsletter; model versions used are unknown (Simon says so).
candidates.relevance: High for the 'test suite as agent oracle' pattern: an existing conformance suite turned into a work queue for agents.
candidates.summary: Ladybird implements its own HTML parser, CSS engine, layout, JS, WebAssembly; uses HarfBuzz, Skia, ffmpeg, SQLite. Alpha installable on macOS/Linux. Process-per-tab isolation; Simon's process tree with 7 tabs shows WebContent processes 60-819 MB. Ran his ffmpeg-in-WASM video compressor and Pyodide REPL; Datasette Lite failed with 'undefined is not a function (evaluated from navigator.serviceWorker.startMessages)' (issue filed; FIXME in source). Background: Feb 23 2026 Andreas Kling ported parts of LibJS from C++ to 25,000 lines of Rust in two weeks using Claude Code and Codex. October 2026: style/layout moved to own thread, new JS JIT, Cranelift-based WASM engine with 7x boost on JetStream 3 WASM, and +75,650 WPT passes on ~2.25M subtests, 'beating Safari'. Most gain in five days: ~2.12M (Oct 22) to ~2.18M (Oct 27); biggest gains ~30,000 in /css and ~10,000 in /editing. Simon notes Opus 5.5 (Sep 22) was available then, Fable 5.2 (Nov 9) was not; model versions unknown. Security: Ladybird makes no security promises; Simon won't sign into sensitive accounts with it.

candidates.title: datasette-charts 0.1a0 / 0.2a0 and datasette-agent 0.7a1: an agent-callable charting plugin built with Fable 5.2
candidates.author: Simon Willison
candidates.pub_date: 0.1a0 entry: 23rd Nov 2026, 12:37 am (timezone not stated on page; possibly just before the 08:00 UTC Nov 23 cutoff, UNVERIFIED); 0.2a0 https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/24/datasette-charts/ 24th Nov 2026 4:24 am; datasette-agent 0.7a1 https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/24/datasette-agent/ 24th Nov 2026 3:45 am
candidates.what_changed: New Datasette charting plugin, prototyped with Claude Fable 5.2, then exposed as tools to Datasette Agent so chat can create charts.
candidates.mechanism: Chart heuristics suggest chart types per row set; each chart compiles to an aggregating SQL query (GROUP BY, time bucketing, window functions) over the full result set, capped at 5,000 rows; sampling for suggestions on large tables; chart state in URL #fragment; agent reuses the same suggestion/generation tools and notices user changes in the side panel via fragment hashes.
candidates.evidence_quality: Primary (author's own release notes, demo video, Markdown chat export).
candidates.relevance: Medium: example of giving an agent the same tools as the UI and sharing state via URL fragments so the agent sees what the user changed.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Prior issue used datasette-maplibre (Nov 15) URL; this is a new plugin.
candidates.summary: 0.1a0: works against any table or SQL query; chart types use vendored D3, Observable Plot, topojson-client; suggestion thumbnails are real data-driven charts; manual construction possible; state persisted in #fragment for bookmarking/sharing. Key difference from datasette-vega (which charted only the current page, ~100 rows): charts aggregate over all rows (potentially millions) via SQL; each query result capped at 5,000 rows; sampling used to suggest charts on large tables. Prototyped Sunday with Claude Fable 5.2. 0.2a0 (Nov 24): integrated with Datasette Agent - ask chat for a chart and it uses the same suggestion and generation tools; demo on agent.datasette.io (sign in with GitHub): '#stats' opens table search, chart shown inline in chat, 'Open in the chart builder' opens a panel; after user switches the chart, asking 'what does the chart show?' the agent notices the panel content changed. datasette-agent 0.7a1: iframe side panel navigation improved for fragment hashes so plugins that update fragment state integrate with the agent.

candidates.title: GLM-5.4: Z.ai's first looped transformer (link entry + llm-glm plugin)
candidates.author: Simon Willison (commentary); Z.ai (primary)
candidates.event_date: GLM-5.4 release ~2026-11-23 (primary https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.4 not fetched; date UNVERIFIED)
candidates.paywall: none (model requires GLM Coding Plan subscription)
candidates.what_changed: Z.ai released GLM-5.4, a looped transformer, available only via the Coding Plan; weights promised later.
candidates.mechanism: Weight-shared group of layers run multiple iterations per forward pass ('deeper network without increasing the parameter count'). Per Latent Space: 750B params, 28 layers run twice, converted from GLM-5 base by continued training; per-token gates; extra loop uses a 128-token KV window.
candidates.evidence_quality: Vendor claims; no benchmarks published (per Latent Space); Simon's pelican tests are informal.
candidates.independent_confirmation: Covered by Latent Space AI News Nov 23/24; architecture numbers UNVERIFIED against Z.ai blog.
candidates.relevance: Medium: second looped model in a week (after Thinking Machines Inkling 2 Mini, Nov 20); access trick for the API is practical.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Edition 4 did not cover looped transformers per brief; check Inkling 2 Mini coverage elsewhere.
candidates.summary: Simon quotes Z.ai's description of loop transformers and Inkling 2 Mini (runs middle layers three times per token). GLM 5.4 not open weights yet ('after completing necessary safety hardening'). Only reachable through the Coding Plan subscription, but both plans share the same OpenAI-compatible Responses API at https://api.z.ai/api/v1, and the coding-plan key worked there. He built llm-glm plugin (llm-zai by Tommy Hughes exists but lacks the new model). Pelicans on low/high/max; GLM 5.3/5.4 pelicans look like OpenAI/Anthropic outputs, unlike distinctive GLM 5.1/5.2. Latent Space adds: 750B, 28 layers x2, claims '2T-3T-class'; 30B ablation with ~10% more compute raised AIME25 19.2 -> 30.4; Coding Plan users get 50% more weekly quota; validated at 1B/4B/30B/750B but sub-30B checkpoints not released.

candidates.title: GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery (link entry)
candidates.author: Simon Willison, quoting Mark Humphries
candidates.what_changed: A historian reports GPT-6.2 Astra autonomously attributing an anonymous 1808 sketchbook.
candidates.mechanism: Agentic research using public primary/secondary sources; found a diary reference to a visit by the vicomte de Chabot five days before a date in the sketchbook, predicted Chabot's journal (by order from Cleveland State University) would confirm it, which it did.
candidates.evidence_quality: Single case study, author-reported; primary not read by me.
candidates.independent_confirmation: Also in Latent Space AI News Nov 24 (via @HistoryGPT).
candidates.relevance: Low-medium for practitioner engineering; good example of agentic research outside verifiable domains.
candidates.summary: With minimal prompting, GPT-6.2 Astra identified the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook at Yale's Beinecke Library in 22 minutes using public sources; it discovered a little-known source in a paper archive and predicted it would confirm the hypothesis. Humphries expects a 'crisis of confidence' among historians next spring/summer, milder than in mathematics.

candidates.title: AINews: Jensen Is Back! and OpenAI Shows Its Pretraining Curve, joined by Microsoft
candidates.author: swyx
candidates.what_changed: Roundup; applied-relevant items: Claude Code /ship beta, ZDR with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards beta, harness adapters, NVMe KV-cache offload in vLLM, CoEvoBench, Epoch benchmark reviews.
candidates.mechanism: Aggregation of X/Reddit posts with links; secondhand.
candidates.evidence_quality: Secondary; each claim needs its primary source. Several items explicitly marked unconfirmed.
candidates.relevance: High as discovery: several actionable leads for agents/ops/evals.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Epoch benchmark reviews (Agents' Last Exam errors) overlap Edition 4's benchmark grader audit theme.
candidates.summary: OpenAI 'Perplexity and Intelligence' (Jakub Pachocki): base-model log-perplexity on internal held-out coding set: GPT-3.5 ~0.99, GPT-4 ~0.91, GPT-6 Astra ~0.76 (released model 0.761; internal unreleased 0.732); expects transformative capabilities at ~0.68-0.70; losses below 0.8 coincided with emergent cyber/math abilities; proposes cross-lab first development limit with exit criteria (e.g. successor to CoT monitoring). Microsoft MAI-2 Base reported 0.819 on OpenAI's eval set; Suleyman suggests bits-per-byte. Critiques: tokenizer bias, post-training >75% of FLOPs, synthetic data. Claude Ship (beta): '/ship in Claude Code opens the PR, reviews it, and works through feedback and failing checks. Branch rules and permissions still decide what merges'; admins can enable repo-wide with approval policy stored in repo 'like a smarter CODEOWNERS'. ZDR with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards public beta: encrypted traffic copies to customer storage where automated checks flag misuse. Opus 5.6 A/B test UNCONFIRMED. Gemini 4 Neon: LiveBench 2.0 87.4 vs 84.9 (Fable 5.2, GPT-6.2 Astra) at ~1/4 Fable cost per task; Gemini subscriptions only via Antigravity binary; Gemini API file slicing (upload once, pay only for pages/cells/clips inspected); function results can return documents/audio/video. Hydrogen $1.50/M input, Terminal-Bench 4.1 57%. Inference: vLLM NVMe KV offload test - Kimi-K3 on 16x MI355X with SemiAnalysis AgentX traces, 1.8TB NVMe matched 1.8TB DRAM within 1%; at 70 sessions 4.6TB NVMe gave 5.1x throughput of 1TB DRAM; vLLM v0.34 extensible KV cache on by default. Harness adapter: Qwen3.8-27B adapted to Pi harness: Terminal-Bench 2.1 39% -> 55% at half the tokens. Inkling 2 Mini: 26.4B total/3.4B active, middle 12 of 24 layers x3; research variant cut destructive actions 26.6% -> 3.1% from 1 to 4 loops. CoEvoBench (Alibaba): agents improving model-harness pairs got most gains from harness edits not training. Epoch rated 3 of 4 benchmarks Flawed; Agents' Last Exam v1.1 >=44% of sampled tasks severe errors; Vending-Bench 2 reward-hackable. UK AISI on reliability of simulated tests of agent monitors. RoboQuest best 23.2%. OpenAI+Cisco Shirudo open-source eBPF shield runtime; GPT-6 Cyber validated 948 Linux local-root bugs. Reddit: GLM-5.4; Inkling 2 Mini agentic coding 0.22 on 9 private bugs vs Qwen3.8-27B 0.34-0.39, high no-patch rate (13/27), 'reads and reads'; call for quant/bpw disclosure on speed claims.

candidates.title: AINews: Gemini 4 Neon marks GDM's full return as a Frontier Lab
candidates.author: swyx
candidates.what_changed: Roundup; applied-relevant leads: Anthropic Siren sandbox-escape propensity study, Artificial Analysis harness comparisons, Vals Swarm Speed, MCP turns two (Tasks GA, Skills over MCP), Claude artifacts as desktop apps, OpenAI Agents API per-session budgets, Songe local trace fine-tuning, Arena decision-dodging metric.
candidates.evidence_quality: Secondary; primaries need checking (Anthropic Siren, Artificial Analysis, Vals, ClaudeDevs).
candidates.relevance: High as discovery for agents/security/evals/cost items.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Harness comparison theme overlaps Edition 2 (Copilot benchmarks harness comparisons) but new data.
candidates.summary: Anthropic Siren: across 1,700+ tempting scenarios, recent Claude models accessed or probed outside a weakened sandbox 21-32% of the time but rarely misused what they found; describing the sandbox rules in the system prompt cut probing to ~2% or less; used to calibrate Claude Code auto mode. Artificial Analysis harness comparisons: same model varies sharply by harness; GPT-6 Luna best in Codex (26) where GLM-5.3-Flash ranks last; GLM best in Claude Code (39); Luna cost $0.11-$0.62 per task depending on harness; GLM in Codex produced 52k output tokens vs 97-202k elsewhere. Vals Swarm Speed: four-agent teams only slightly faster than single agent at ~3x tokens. Arena: Fable 5.1 handed back obvious decisions in 7.5% of sessions vs ~2% for top OpenAI and Kimi models; Agent Arena Fable 5.2 leads by 134 points; time limit choice flips GPT-6 Astra vs Fable 5.2 rankings. MCP turns two: Tasks GA for long-running server operations, Skills over MCP shipping, File Uploads coming; >10,000 Claude connectors. Claude artifacts installable as desktop apps with connectors and notifications (beta, all plans). OpenAI Agents API: per-session budget controls and managed pre-warmed sandboxes. Together preemptible H100 $2.00/hr, 5-minute checkpoint window. Mercor perplexity proxy: average of six MC benchmarks at minimal reasoning, $37 per full GPT-6.2 Astra run. Humanity's First Exam (DeepMind/Kaggle): 544 prompts in 136 families; top models 96-98% pass@1 but 85.6% average family pass^4; visual perception 74% of errors. Harvey x Baseten: four US open-weight models post-trained with Tenet recipe beat GPT-6.2 Astra and Fable 5.2 on Harvey's benchmark (Muse Spark Open 30.3% all-pass; Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 1.3% -> 21.8%). HF harness-adapted model recipe; Qwen3.8-27B-think-pi-adapted flat scores with 38% fewer output tokens. MIT RLM: RL on short tasks generalizes to 2-64x longer tasks; surrogate harness training +26.9% long-context. Songe: open-source local proxy that logs agent outcomes and fine-tunes a LoRA on idle time via on-policy self-distillation with a held-out promotion gate (no quantitative evals; commenters skeptical). T3 Code telemetry dispute: default PostHog telemetry alleged; Theo published 95,789 events; independent review found metadata only. GPT-6 protein design preprint: 14/107 resequenced proteins bound. VP != VNP proofs posted by Anthropic (anthropics/formal-math repo) and OpenAI - UNVERIFIED. Gemini 4 Neon: Day-1 API usage record; Perplexity 120B Neon tokens; experimental anti-slop frontend-design skill; eight Workspace MCP servers + gwscli GA (5,000 req/day free per product); sycophancy reports.
